entries.rationale: Offline foundation verifier: the match is a privacy deny-list over sealed receipt text; it neither extracts credentials nor invokes a provider.
Offline evidence mutation suite: credential-shaped words occur only in synthetic JSON fixtures and local receipt-copy tests; no provider command is born.
Sourced pure boundary predicates compare caller-supplied historical strings; this file performs no credential read, extraction, copy, or provider execution.
Offline historical-source regression: it reads committed script text and uses an invented command behind an unconditional guard; it cannot reach auth, network, or provider paths.
Offline receipt mutation suite: matched terms are JSON claim fixtures and file-copy setup, with no credential source access or provider process invocation.
Offline historical receipt/SSOT verifier: matched credential text is parsed claim metadata only; the verifier does not read credentials or invoke a provider.
Historical source assertion suite: its only runner target is now an exact unconditional refusal stub; matched token/extraction forms are expected-text assertions.
Offline disposition mutation suite: LOGIN_ACCEPTED is a rejected JSON fixture value, not a command or process invocation.
Offline sealed-receipt verifier: matched credential terms occur in jq assertions and privacy refusal patterns; no credential or provider operation occurs.
Historical poison-marker test: its probe target is now an exact unconditional refusal stub, so ambient synthetic token variables are never read or transported.
Pure offline policy parser: browser/OAuth forms are prohibited-text matchers over supplied documents and cannot launch a browser or provider process.
This offline scanner contains only detection regular expressions for the matched forms; its sole subprocess is git ls-files and it has no provider interface.
Offline policy mutation suite: provider-login, browser, and credential phrases are inert document fixtures consumed only by the Ruby validator.
Offline scanner mutation suite: every matched form is written as inert source into disposable Git fixtures and is never executed as an auth, browser, or provider command.
Offline receipt checker: matched terms are sealed evidence labels and JSON equality assertions; it invokes Git/JQ/hash tools only and no provider interface.
Offline receipt checker: access-token flags are exact rejected-selector evidence assertions; the script reads no credential value and exposes no provider interface.
Offline historical receipt verifier: credential terms occur only in a deny-list privacy scan over committed evidence; no auth input or provider process is used.
Offline historical placement verifier: the match is a deny-list privacy scan over sealed evidence and performs no credential extraction or provider login.
Historical negative-context verifier: matched credential text is a privacy deny-list; its provider call is version-only and contains no auth or login route.
Offline static-context verifier: matched credential terms are privacy deny-list literals over receipts, with no provider or authentication subprocess.
Historical rooted-disposition verifier: the match is a receipt privacy deny-list and the script exposes no auth-file, token-input, or provider-login route.
Compiled state code contains a deny-list that rejects saved arguments with token/API-key/password spellings; it never reads environment credentials or starts a process.
